name: Southwestern Nisu
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog marks the entry probably spurious/confused (points to Southern Nisu [nsd]); only Nisu dialect surveys (Chan et al. 2008; Yang 2009) cited, none for this variety.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1 languoid record sout3128 (Southwestern Nisu), with Hammarström's Ethnologue comment
sources.note: Bookkeeping; 'SW Nisu, as a distinct variety spoken in Pu'er or in Xishuangbanna prefecture, is not taken up in Nisu dialect surveys.. The SW Nisu entry is therefore probably spurious, or seriously confused.' Only reference = CR 2007-086.

sources.citation: Lama, Ziwo Qiu-Fuyuan. 2012. Subgrouping of Nisoic (Yi) Languages: A Study from the Perspectives of Shared Innovation and Phylogenetic Estimation. PhD diss., University of Texas at Arlington. 399 pp. hdl 10106/11161.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: a digital copy exists, behind a library sign-in
sources.note: pp. 77-78 profile 'Nisu 尼苏 (Jiangcheng)/ Nishu 尼蜀 (Xinping)': 'Nisu [ne̠33su55(pho21)] (or the Southwest vernacular spoken in Jiangcheng area).. The Nisu in Jiangcheng County has 34 initial consonants, 22 vowels.. and three tones (/55/, /33/, and /21/)' (cf. YYFC 1983). The words stress/accent occur 0 times in the text: SILENT.

sources.citation: Yang, Cathryn. 2009. Nisu Dialect Geography. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2009-007. 40 pp. Dallas: SIL International.
sources.note: sec. 1.3 (pp. 5-6) pan-Nisu phonemic inventory: tones High 55 / Mid 33 / Low 21, tense/lax vowels. sec. 1.5 (p. 8): 'Nisu varieties spoken in Jiangcheng, Mojiang, and Lvchun counties are found to linguistically affiliate with NC, not with S' (i.e. the [nsv] area is filed under North-Central Nisu = [nos]); App. 1 datapoints JC GQ, MJ MN, MJ JX, LC NK = NC. The words stress/accent do not occur anywhere: SILENT.

sources.citation: Chan, Ken, Bai Bibo & Yang Liujin. 2008. Language Use and Language Attitudes among Rural Nisu. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2008-017. 29 pp.
sources.note: Sociolinguistic questionnaire study; Mojiang Mengnong Malishu and Jiangcheng Guoqing Sanjiacun are two of its 14 villages. No phonology: SILENT.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2007. Change Request 2007-086 (Cathryn Yang; Eric Johnson, Jamin Pelkey, Ken Chan): split [yym] Yuanjiang-Mojiang Yi into Nisu, Southern [nsd] and Nisu, Southwestern [nsv]. 8 pp.
sources.note: Identity only: 2006 RTT survey (Chan & Yang); SW Nisu speakers 'were unable to adequately comprehend any of the other Nisu varieties'; 'the speakers moved away from the Northern Nisu area several generations ago to the southwest'. Nothing on phonology or stress.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2007. Request for New Language Code Element: Nisu, Southwestern [nsv] (CR 2007-086). 5 pp.
sources.note: Identity only: autonym Nisu 尼苏; 'Yunnan province, in Jiangcheng, Simao, Mojiang, Lüchun (western), and Pu'er counties'; ~15,000 speakers (2004); no published sources listed. Nothing on stress.
Tertiary identity only: 西南尼苏语 15,000 in 墨江、江城、思茅、宁洱、绿春西部 = Zhu Wenxu's 墨江次土语; Yang's NC group '即东尼苏语和西南尼苏语'. No stress statement.
